chunks.arabic_text: سَالِمُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، أَبُو عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، الْأَشْلُ. ثِقَةٌ. رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَر، وَأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: Sālim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, al-Ashl. Thiqah. Narrated from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon them).

en.summary: This entry highlights Sālim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, known as al-Ashl, as a trustworthy (thiqah) narrator within the Shia chain of transmission, specifically linking him to the second and third Imams, al-Baqir and al-Sadiq. His designation as 'thiqah' underscores the rigorous scrutiny applied to narrators in Shia hadith sciences, ensuring the authenticity of teachings derived from the Ahl al-Bayt. The mention of his kunya, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, further aids in distinguishing him from other contemporaries in the vast corpus of Shia biographical dictionaries.
en.seo_question: Who is Sālim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ashl and who did he narrate from?
